nina: Heads-up: sample edge app fails with 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' and TS autocomplete shows client.invoke(...) as 'any'.
omar: Which import path are you using? ESM/CJS ambiguity is common.
nina: `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` inside a Cloudflare Worker.
jay: Probable cause: bundler resolved the require (CJS) entry. Check package.json "exports" for explicit "import" mapping.
maya: Also check tsconfig. If moduleResolution is "node" some bundlers pick the wrong entry. For workers set `moduleResolution: "bundler"` and `module: "ESNext"`.
ci-bot: CI alert: edge-integration job failed yesterday, creating ticket.
omar: For types: our d.ts had overlapping overloads where one fallback returned unknown/any. That makes inference collapse. Short term, annotate `await client.invoke<MyType>(...)`.
jay: Longer term: change public typings to a single generic signature e.g. `invoke<T = JsonValue>(opts): Promise<T>` and avoid fallback overloads. Also publish a `./worker` export so workers don't accidentally hit CJS.
nina: I updated sample app locally: added "./worker": { "import": "./dist/esm/worker-entry.mjs", "types": "./dist/worker.d.ts" } to exports and switched tsconfig to bundler. Runtime error gone; types better but I still annotated one call with `<T>` to get full shape.
maya: Good incremental fix. Follow-ups: PR for typings change, PR for worker export, add sample-app README snippet with minimal tsconfig, and add a CI bundling test for worker target.
omar: I'll open the typings PR to prefer a single generic and change default to `JsonValue`.
ci-bot: Linked issues: #780 #781.
nina: Thanks — this saved the workshop demo.
